I wrote `totals_by_category` in `totals.rb`; I haven't run it.

```ruby
def totals_by_category(items)
  items.each_with_object(Hash.new(0)) do |item, totals|
    totals[item[:category]] += item[:amount]
  end
end
```

For example, `totals_by_category([{ category: "food", amount: 12 }, { category: "food", amount: 3 }, { category: "rent", amount: 900 }])` returns `{ "food" => 15, "rent" => 900 }`.

The returned hash has a default of 0, so looking up a category that isn't present gives `0` rather than `nil`.
